rustdesk.title: RustDesk Server
rustdesk.intro: Integrate RustDesk Server (open source): install the dedicated RustDesk agent (not a scan agent) on the RustDesk host. It reads the registered devices and their online state, receives the host name, OS and connection audit reported by the clients, and sends them to jt-ipam. Once a device is mapped to an IP record, you can open a RustDesk session from the IP page.
rustdesk.step_create: Click Add to create the RustDesk server. A dedicated agent key and install command are generated for it.
rustdesk.privacy: The agent only sends the ID, first registration time, registered IP, online state, hbbs version and public key, the host name, OS, signed-in user and connection records the clients report themselves, and which IPs the hbbr/hbbs logs show refused for the Key or passing the relay (only the IP, time and count, never the log text). It never opens the private key file and never changes any RustDesk setting. Client uuids are only compared on the RustDesk host and never sent to jt-ipam.
rustdesk.confirm_delete: Delete this server? Its device list, IP mappings and connection audit are deleted too, and the agent key stops working.
rustdesk.client_address_hint: The domain or IP clients use to reach this server (may include :port). When set, "Connect with RustDesk" passes this address and the public key, so the client needs no prior setup; when empty, the client uses the server it is configured with.
rustdesk.search_ph: Search ID, IP or host name
rustdesk.no_devices: No devices yet (waiting for the agent; you can use Sync now).
rustdesk.connect_hint: Connect to {id} with the RustDesk client (RustDesk must be installed on this computer)
rustdesk.match_matched_hint: An IP signal (report source IP or registered IP) maps to exactly one IP record, the device was online within 7 days, and the host name does not contradict it.
rustdesk.match_not_seen_online_hint: jt-ipam has not seen it online yet; an offline device's registered IP may be old, so it is not mapped.
rustdesk.match_stale_hint: Not online for more than 7 days; the registered IP may belong to another machine by now, so it is not mapped.
rustdesk.match_shared_hint: Three or more IDs registered with the same IP, so there is no telling which is which. Usually NAT reflection (every client appears to come from the firewall), or a DHCP address that has gone to several machines running RustDesk over the years.
rustdesk.match_ambiguous_hint: Two devices are online on the same IP, or the IP has two records in overlapping subnets; no guessing.
rustdesk.match_unmanaged_hint: The registered IP is not in any jt-ipam IP record (e.g. a public address on an outside network).
rustdesk.match_no_ip_hint: The RustDesk server has no IP for this device.
rustdesk.match_conflict_hint: The record the registered IP points to has a different host name from the one this device reports, and no recent heartbeat came from that address. Usually the DHCP address now belongs to another machine, so it is not mapped.
rustdesk.match_hostname_only_hint: The IP is not in our networks, but the host name matches exactly one record (e.g. a company laptop on a home connection). Shown as a suggestion, not mapped.
rustdesk.reports_hint: Clients without an API server send their reports to port {port} of the ID server, where the RustDesk agent receives them.
rustdesk.receive_reports_hint: When on, the RustDesk agent listens on this port on the RustDesk host and receives client heartbeats, system info, connection and file transfer audits and alarms. Clients with the API server left empty already send to port 21114 of the ID server, so no client change is needed. ⚠️ Do not open this port to the internet (reports need no login, so anyone could send fake data): internal networks only, with outside clients on a VPN or restricted by source IP.
rustdesk.audit_empty: No audit records yet (turn on "Receive client reports" and make sure clients can reach the agent).
rustdesk.unverified_hint: A note from the controlling side carries no uuid, so only the existence of the ID was checked.
rustdesk.alarm_6: Too many failures from one IPv6 prefix
rustdesk.step_install: Run the install command as root on the RustDesk host (where hbbs runs). The agent reads the official working directory read-only:
rustdesk.step_test: When the agent column shows Connected, click Test to check the database, the online query and the client report receiver one by one; Sync now reads once right away.
rustdesk.step_reports: Clients that only have the ID server set (API server left empty) send their host name, OS and connection audit to TCP {port} on the RustDesk host, where the agent receives them. No client change is needed. ⚠️ Do not open this port to the internet: it accepts client reports without any login, so anyone could send fake reports and alarms. Open it to internal networks only; have outside clients use a VPN, or restrict source IPs on the firewall.
rustdesk.agent_install_hint: No agent has connected yet: use Install command in the actions column and run it on the RustDesk host.
rustdesk.sync_queued: Agent notified; it reads and reports within {n} seconds.
rustdesk.sync_queued_offline: Queued, but the agent is not connected; it runs when the agent connects.
rustdesk.test_waiting: Waiting for the agent to check the RustDesk host (it polls every {n} seconds)…
rustdesk.test_timeout: The agent did not respond within {n} seconds.
rustdesk.test_never: The agent has never connected to jt-ipam: run the install command on the RustDesk host first.
rustdesk.install_created: Created. Run the install command below on the RustDesk host. The key is stored encrypted; you can see it again with Install command in the actions column.
rustdesk.install_where: Run as root on the RustDesk host where hbbs runs (one line):
rustdesk.install_dir_hint: If hbbs does not use /var/lib/rustdesk-server, add JT_IPAM_RUSTDESK_DIR=<path> after env. The agent runs as the owner of that directory and mounts it read-only; it never changes any RustDesk file.
rustdesk.rotate_confirm: The old key stops working immediately and the agent on the RustDesk host must be reinstalled with the new command. Continue?
rustdesk.rotated: New key generated. Run the install command on the RustDesk host again.
rustdesk.no_key: This server has no agent key yet (created by an older version that used a scan agent). Generate a key, then install the dedicated agent with the command below.
rustdesk.key_warn: One key per RustDesk server. Whoever has the key can send data as this server; if it leaks, use New key.
rustdesk.enable_hint: When enabled, authorized users can connect with RustDesk from this IP's detail page: directly in the browser when the RustDesk server allows web connections, or by opening the RustDesk client installed on their own computer (this IP must be mapped to a RustDesk device).
rustdesk.elsewhere_hint: This IP is not mapped to a RustDesk device. When a computer has several IPs, RustDesk maps only to the address it connects from; this device's RustDesk is mapped to the IP below, so turn it on there:
rustdesk.badge_local_tip: Opens the RustDesk client installed on your computer, not the jt-ipam web page
rustdesk.candidate_tip: Host name on the IP record: {host}
rustdesk.web_connect: Connect with RustDesk in the browser
rustdesk.web_connect_hint: Connect to {id} in the browser through the RustDesk server (no RustDesk install needed)
rustdesk.web_enabled_hint: When on, users with remote console rights can operate mapped devices directly in the browser (RustDesk-compatible web connection). The jt-ipam server connects to this server's hbbs (rendezvous) and hbbr (relay) and only relays encrypted data; passwords and the screen stay in the user's browser. hbbs must run with its key file (KEY=_ in the .env of the official deb), otherwise web connections are refused.
rustdesk.hbbs_host_hint: Host name or IP the jt-ipam server uses to reach hbbs (optional :port). Empty means the source address reported by the agent.
rustdesk.relay_host_ph: Empty = the hbbs host plus the default relay port
rustdesk.relay_host_hint: Address the jt-ipam server uses to reach hbbr (optional :port); it must be the same hbbr the devices use. Check this carefully when hbbs is configured with several relays.
rustdesk.transport_hint: How the jt-ipam server talks to hbbs/hbbr. TCP is the default (ports 21116/21117 are always open); WebSocket uses 21118/21119.
rustdesk.web_file_transfer_hint: When on, people with RustDesk connection rights on an IP can use “File transfer” in the ▾ menu of the RustDesk button on the IP page to transfer files in the browser. It is a separate connection: the backend relays encrypted data only and never sees the files, and file actions are audited as reported by the browser. The remote device must also allow file transfer. Off by default.
rustdesk.web_file_limits_hint: Files over the limit are not uploaded (checked by the browser). Defaults: 2048 MB per file, 10240 MB per upload.
rustdesk.key_problem_hint: The relay server refused this device at {at} ({n} times since it last passed): its RustDesk Key differs from the server's. It still registers and reports, and direct connections on the same LAN work, but the web connection and connections from outside fail.
rustdesk.key_problem_hint_hbbs: The ID server refused a connection from this device at {at} ({n} times since it last passed): its RustDesk Key differs from the server's, so connecting from it to other devices fails.
rustdesk.key_problem_fix: On this computer, set the Key in RustDesk "Settings → Network → ID/Relay server" to exactly the server's public key (copy and paste it; it is case-sensitive).
rustdesk.key_problems_hint: These devices' RustDesk Key differs from the server's (the RustDesk agent saw them refused in the relay server's log). Click to list them
rustdesk.check_logs: hbbr/hbbs logs (finds clients with a wrong Key)
rustdesk.open_local_client: Open in the RustDesk client software on this computer
rustdesk.open_local_client_tip: Opens the RustDesk client software installed on this computer and connects to {id}, not through the jt-ipam web page (RustDesk must be installed)
rustdesk.open_files_tip: Open file transfer in a new tab (transfer files in the browser over a separate connection through the RustDesk server; ID {id})
rustdesk.allow_peer_delete_hint: When on, offline devices can be ticked on the Devices tab and the RustDesk agent deletes their registrations from the hbbs database. The RustDesk host must also re-run the install command with --allow-delete (the install command includes it) before the agent can write; without it the hbbs directory stays read-only for the agent. Right before deleting, the agent checks the online state again and never deletes a device that is online; a device registers again by itself when it next comes online (same ID). Turning this off cancels deletions that are still waiting.
rustdesk.install_allow_delete: This server allows deleting old registrations, so the install command carries JT_RD_ALLOW_DELETE=1: only then can the agent write to the hbbs database (it deletes only registrations in the peer table, and the private key file is hidden from it). On a host where the agent is already installed, run this line to switch it on (the URL and key already on the host are kept):
rustdesk.install_read_only_hint: This server does not allow deleting old registrations: the install command has no JT_RD_ALLOW_DELETE and the hbbs directory is read-only for the agent (re-running this command on a host installed with --allow-delete makes it read-only again).
rustdesk.agent_cap_unknown: Not reported by the agent yet (needs 1.2.0 or later; it updates itself)
rustdesk.check_peer_delete_off: Read-only (deleting old registrations is not enabled on the host; this is the default)
rustdesk.del_pick: Tick the offline devices to delete (online devices cannot be ticked)
rustdesk.del_tip: Delete the {n} ticked registrations from the RustDesk server
rustdesk.del_off: "Allow deleting old registrations" is off for this server: edit the server on the RustDesk servers tab.
rustdesk.del_agent_unknown: The RustDesk agent has not reported write access yet (it needs 1.2.0 or later and must be connected; it updates itself).
rustdesk.del_agent_cannot: The agent on the RustDesk host has no write access: {reason}. Re-run the install command with --allow-delete on the RustDesk host ("Install command" in the actions column).
rustdesk.del_capped: At most {n} can be deleted at a time; only the first {n} are ticked.
rustdesk.del_confirm: Delete {n} registrations from the RustDesk server "{server}"?
rustdesk.del_note_online: Right before deleting, the RustDesk agent checks the online state again; devices that are online are skipped and not deleted.
rustdesk.del_note_return: Only the registration in the hbbs database is deleted. RustDesk on the device is not affected and registers again by itself when it next comes online (same ID).
rustdesk.del_note_memory: Devices that connected since hbbs last started are still in its memory and can still be reached, but they reappear in the list only after hbbs restarts and they come online again.
rustdesk.del_queued: {n} queued; the RustDesk agent handles them within about {s} seconds.
rustdesk.del_queued_offline: {n} queued, but the agent is not connected; they run once it connects (after a day without running they count as failed).
rustdesk.del_summary: Delete old registrations: {deleted} deleted, {skipped} skipped (online), {not_found} not found, {failed} failed
rustdesk.del_slow: The agent has not finished yet; see "Deletion log" for the results later.

rdfile.drives_hint: This is the list of drives on the remote device. Open a drive before uploading or creating a folder.

rdfile.drop_dirs_skipped: Uploading folders is not supported yet; skipped {n} folder(s)
rdfile.disconnect_confirm: Some transfers have not finished, and disconnecting cancels them. Disconnect anyway?

rdfile.conflict_theirs_time: File on the remote device: {size}, modified {time}
rdfile.conflict_identical: The remote device compared size and modification time: the content looks identical.
rdfile.delete_dir_body: This deletes {name} together with all files and subfolders in it, on the remote device. It cannot be undone.
rdfile.err_no_permission: The remote device has not turned on its file transfer permission, so it refused this connection. Turn on file transfer in the RustDesk settings on the remote device (Security, Permissions), or use the remote desktop instead.

rdfile.err_peer: The remote device reported an error: {reason}
rdfile.err_timeout: The remote device did not respond; refresh and try again
rdfile.err_too_large: Over the upload limit set on the server
rdfile.err_read: Cannot read the local file (it may have been moved, or there is no read permission)

rdfile.err_protocol: The remote device sent data out of order, so the transfer was stopped

rdweb.connect_to: Connect to {ip} through the RustDesk server
rdweb.password_note: Leave empty to ask the person at the remote computer to accept instead. The password is hashed inside this browser tab and never sent to the jt-ipam server.
rdweb.password_note_remember: Leave empty to ask the person at the remote computer to accept instead (an empty password is not remembered). After a successful login the password is stored encrypted on the jt-ipam server.
rdweb.view_only_hint: Watch the screen only; no keyboard or mouse input is sent.
rdweb.no_store_hint: The password is used only for this session and is not stored on the server.
rdweb.cred_manual: Use a different password (enter it below)
rdweb.use_saved_hint: Using the saved password: stored encrypted on the server; only at connect time the backend computes a hash valid for this connection alone, and the password is never sent to the browser.
rdweb.store_hint: When on, the password is stored encrypted on the server for this IP only once the login succeeds (only you can use it; plaintext is never returned); reusable next time. Nothing is stored if the login fails.
rdweb.password_saved: Password remembered; you will not need to type it next time
rdweb.reconnect_otp_hint: The device switched sessions, so its one-time password may have changed. Enter the new password.
rdweb.login_screen_hint: The device is at its login screen. Enter the password.
rdweb.login_err_wayland_login: The device is at a Wayland login screen, which cannot be controlled remotely. Switch the device to an X11 login screen, or log in locally first (see {url})
rdweb.login_err_another_user: Another user is already logged in on the device
rdweb.login_err_xorg_missing: Xorg is not installed on the device
rdweb.login_err_no_desktop: The device has no desktop environment
rdweb.os_login_title: The device has no desktop yet. Enter an OS account to log in.
rdweb.os_login_note: The OS account is used only for this login (sent to the device inside the encrypted channel). It is not stored and is not sent again when reconnecting.
rdweb.os_err_xsession: The OS login or the desktop start failed. Enter the account again.
rdweb.os_err_rd_password: Wrong RustDesk password. Enter the OS account and the RustDesk password again.
rdweb.win_session_title: Choose the Windows session to connect to

rdweb.stage_relay: Waiting for the device to join the relay…
rdweb.cad_hint: Send Ctrl+Alt+Del (browsers do not let a web page capture this combination)
rdweb.keyboard_blocked: The remote side has turned off control; you can only watch for now.
rdweb.elev_tag_hint: A portable (not installed) RustDesk cannot control windows running as administrator or the UAC prompt. For now you can use "Request elevation".

rdweb.elev_foreground: The window in front on the remote computer runs as administrator, and a portable RustDesk cannot send keyboard or mouse input to it. Ask the person there to move it to the background, or request elevation.
rdweb.elev_uac: The remote computer is showing a UAC prompt. It cannot be seen or clicked from here, so the person at that computer has to answer it. After elevating with an administrator account you can operate it from here.
rdweb.elev_direct: Confirm on the remote computer (someone there clicks "Yes" in UAC)

rdweb.elev_logon_user: Administrator account on the remote computer
rdweb.elev_logon_note: The account and password are sent encrypted straight to the remote computer; the jt-ipam server cannot see them. They are not remembered and are cleared as soon as you submit. Nobody needs to be at the remote computer for this method.
rdweb.elev_sent_direct: Sent: ask the person at the remote computer to click "Yes" in the UAC window
rdweb.elev_sent_logon: Sent: waiting for the remote computer to start it…
rdweb.elev_ok: Elevated: windows running as administrator and the UAC prompt can now be controlled
rdweb.elev_err_no_permission: The remote computer does not allow keyboard control, so it cannot be elevated ({raw})

rdweb.clip_sent: Put on the remote clipboard ({n} characters). Press Ctrl+V on the remote computer to paste.

isoinsight.title: ISOinsight integration
isoinsight.intro: Logs in to the ISOinsight HTTP(S) interface and reads its DHCP leases on a schedule, merging them into IP, MAC, host name and source records. It only logs in and reads; it never changes DHCP settings or leases on the device.
isoinsight.step_create: Add a source: host, credentials, login method and source time zone
isoinsight.step_test: Test the connection: login and lease reading, step by step
isoinsight.step_preview: Preview the leases and subnet matching (not applied)
isoinsight.step_scope: Confirm the customer and the subnets that may be synced
isoinsight.step_sync: Sync once by hand, check the result, then turn the schedule on
isoinsight.unverified_note: Pending verification on a real device: the login response (cookie or token), whether GET or POST works, whether the lease list is complete, and the time zone have not been confirmed on ISOinsight yet. These settings are compatibility options, not a vendor specification.
isoinsight.base_url_hint: For example https://192.0.2.10, without credentials, query or fragment. The login and lease paths are relative to it.
isoinsight.method_hint: GET and POST are explicit choices and never switch automatically (sending credentials repeatedly can lock the account). Verify against the device.
isoinsight.get_warning: GET login puts the credentials in the URL query, so the device or a reverse proxy may record them in its access log. jt-ipam always masks the login query in its own logs.
isoinsight.auth_hold_hint: The last login failed, so the schedule is paused to avoid sending wrong credentials again and again. Editing the settings or a successful test releases it.
isoinsight.tls_off_hint: Certificate verification is off for this source (the change is in the audit log).
isoinsight.confirm_delete: Delete this source? IP records it created stay; the lease flags and host names it reported are withdrawn.
isoinsight.raw_time_hint: The time sent by the source could not be parsed with the current format; the original text is shown and never read as permanent.
isoinsight.product_version_ph: Optional, for example the version the customer reported
isoinsight.password_kept: Keep the current password (tick the box to change it)
isoinsight.scope_customer_hint: All allowed subnets must belong to this customer; matching never crosses customers.
isoinsight.scope_subnets_hint: Matching happens only inside these subnets (longest prefix). A lease that cannot be matched to exactly one subnet is left unmatched, never guessed.
isoinsight.create_ips_hint: An IP record is created only when the lease matches exactly one allowed subnet and is within its lease period; addresses in a cool-down period and network or broadcast addresses are skipped. Off: only existing IP records are updated.
isoinsight.timezone_confirm: I have confirmed the device uses this time zone
isoinsight.timezone_hint: Lease times are converted from this time zone to UTC; the time zone of the jt-ipam host is never used instead.
isoinsight.tls_off_warning: With verification off the device certificate is not checked and credentials could be intercepted. Use it only for a self-signed certificate on a trusted network; the change is recorded in the audit log.
isoinsight.schedule_hint: Uses the jt-ipam schedule (checked every 5 minutes); manual and scheduled runs share one lock.
isoinsight.schedule_needs_preview: No successful preview with the current settings yet: the schedule stays on but does not sync until a preview succeeds.
isoinsight.schedule_after_create: After adding, test and preview; the schedule starts syncing once a preview succeeds.
isoinsight.paths_hint: Paths must be relative to the Base URL and cannot point at another host.
isoinsight.auth_mode_hint: Cookie session by default. Token mode needs an explicit field path and header; nothing is guessed.
isoinsight.token_hint: For example data.token. This is only an example, not a field confirmed by the vendor. The prefix may be empty.
isoinsight.test_not_applied: This is a test result and is not applied: no IP or lease data is written.
isoinsight.preview_not_applied: This is a preview and is not applied: it shows what would be created or applied; no IP or lease data is written.
isoinsight.anonymous_check: Also check whether leases can be read without logging in (manual diagnosis, never scheduled)
isoinsight.probe_ok: Connection and reading succeeded: {fetched} rows, {valid} valid, {invalid} invalid.
isoinsight.anonymous_readable: Leases can be read without logging in: whether authentication is required is not confirmed, and this is not evidence that the credentials are correct.
isoinsight.anonymous_blocked: Leases cannot be read without logging in (HTTP {status}).

technitium.title: Technitium DHCP
technitium.intro: jt-ipam reads Technitium's DHCP scopes, reservations, client options (gateway, DNS, NTP, WINS) and leases: scopes become DHCP pools, reservations go to DHCP reservations, and leases only tag existing IPs (lease, MAC, host name) without creating IPs. For DNS records, add a Technitium server under "DNS servers".
technitium.setup_hint: In Technitium, create a dedicated user and group with view permission for DHCP, sign in as that user and create an API token from the user menu (it does not expire). jt-ipam only reads and needs no modify permission.
technitium.api_url_hint: The Technitium web console, by default http://host:5380 or https://host:53443. If HTTP redirects to HTTPS, enter the HTTPS URL.
technitium.test_ok: Connected: Technitium {version}, account {user}; {scopes} scopes ({enabled} enabled), {leases} active leases
technitium.can_modify: This token can modify DHCP. jt-ipam only reads; an account with view permission only is recommended.
technitium.scopes_hint: Scopes seen by the last sync. Disabled scopes are not written as pools or reservations; the gateway, DNS, NTP and WINS handed to clients are used by IP change assessment (changing those addresses affects the clients in the scope).
